assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another by chemistry on DNA in situ, without double-strand breaks. It is a clear game-changer: a genuinely new chemical tool that has already moved into clinical trials and become standard in research.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the decisive intellectual driver. Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, which needed directed evolution of a new deaminase) did the key experimental work as Liu-lab members. Kondo and Nishida's independent deaminase-fusion work is a real priority question I cannot fully resolve from the supplied credit. Three names are possible but Liu-centred.
assessment.maturity: Roughly ten years old, with broad independent adoption and first clinical results. Timing is plausible, though the clinical record is still young.
uncertainties: Whether Kondo/Nishida's Target-AID deserves a place within the three-person limit.
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy data are limited.
Possible overlap with Medicine or a combined prize with prime editing (B038).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced degradation of target proteins through E3 ligase recruitment opens a new pharmacological modality. It reaches 'undruggable' targets and has real consequences in the clinic, with several PROTACs in late-stage trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (2001) and Crews developed the small-molecule versions. Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL ligands and mechanistic work. The molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a separate lineage with partly different credit. Cutting this to three people is hard and contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and clinical momentum. Approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages may need different recognition.
Priority and credit split between Crews, Deshaies and the thalidomide-mechanism discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of cells is a conceptual shift that unites physical chemistry with cell biology. The impact is large, though the physiological significance is argued case by case.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman (P granules, 2009) are the clear originators. Rosen (multivalent signalling assemblies, 2012) is the most credible third. Pappu and Mittag supply the sequence-grammar theory and are strong contenders, so the three-person cap forces an unfair exclusion.
assessment.maturity: Very fast growth, but there is still debate over in-cell relevance, artefacts of overexpression and definitions. Possibly early.
uncertainties: Fair attribution among five prominent names.
May be seen as more biology or medicine than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made ab initio dynamics practical, so bond breaking, solvation and condensed-phase chemistry could be simulated from electronic structure. It has had lasting impact across chemistry, materials science and biochemistry, and it links directly to experiment.
assessment.attribution: Car and Parrinello's 1985 paper is a precise, unambiguous two-person attribution. No dispute is apparent.
assessment.maturity: Forty years old, fully mature and widely validated. Recognition is overdue. Computation was rewarded in 2013 (multiscale models) and 2024 (protein design), so the field has precedent.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to pair Parrinello with metadynamics (B039) or machine-learned potentials (B049).
Some may judge the work as method development closer to physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel picture resolved Levinthal's paradox, and quantitative experiment (phi-value analysis) then tested it. This is theory tied to experiment, which I consider the core test. It has reshaped thinking about folding, binding and function.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central theorists (with Bryngelson). Fersht supplies the experimental mapping of transition states. Dill's contributions (hydrophobic collapse, lattice models) are important but make a fourth name. Choosing three is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Decades old and well established, though much of its influence is conceptual. Recognition was partly overshadowed by the 2024 protein structure prediction prize.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill, Fersht and Bryngelson.
Whether the contribution is seen as concept more than discovery or invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase (FeMo-cofactor, interstitial carbide, intermediates trapped in turnover) concern one of the most important and difficult reactions in biology and agriculture. It is a deep enzymology problem with high impact.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallography and the cofactor structures, and Einsle solved the central atom and cofactor details. Seefeldt (and Dean) contributed the mechanism, with Ribbe in spectroscopy and biosynthesis. The credit is spread over many contributors and a fair prize is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the full catalytic mechanism is still not settled. Recognition may be early for mechanism, though the structural work is mature.
uncertainties: The mechanism of N2 reduction is unresolved.
Credit is diffuse across several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled the siRNA and mRNA drugs, with a very large and demonstrated real-world consequence including the COVID-19 vaccines. This is a delivery technology, so the chemistry is the key enabler.
assessment.attribution: The Cullis group in Vancouver (Cullis, Hope, Madden) did the foundational lipid-nanoparticle work. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed lipid design and delivery. The assignment is complicated and partly a patent and company question.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed. The 2023 Medicine prize to Karikó and Weissman for modified nucleosides in mRNA makes a Chemistry prize for delivery plausible but could look duplicative.
uncertainties: Contested credit among the Vancouver group, Anderson, Langer and company scientists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis changed biology and medicine, and it was chemistry-led (reversible terminator chemistry, clustered arrays). Impact is exceptional and unquestioned.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry. Mayer (clonal arrays) is a strong third. Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing) and Ju (terminator chemistry) are also credited, so there is a real priority dispute and several parallel inventions.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with enormous independent confirmation, perhaps even overdue. The multi-lineage story makes a three-person split hard.
uncertainties: Multiple parallel technologies (Solexa, 454, SBS by Ju) complicate fair credit.
Part of the sequencing field was recognised in 1980 (Sanger).
